lines.text: Most mid-size IPOs pay banks exactly 7%. So why take a tenth of that?

lines.text: 0.7% of $75 billion is still about $500 million.

Then on day one, the stock jumped nineteen percent, from a hundred thirty-five dollars to about a hundred sixty-one.

lines.text: That handed the investors banks picked about $14.4 billion in one day, almost 30x the fees.

lines.text: Those big investors are also the banks' trading clients.
lines.say: And those big investors are also the banks' trading clients, paying fees on trades all year.

lines.say: At Goldman Sachs in twenty twenty-five, all stock underwriting was about three percent of revenue.

post.title: SpaceX paid bankers 0.7%. Why did banks say yes?
post.ig:
SpaceX raised $75 billion and paid its bankers about 0.7%.
Most mid-size IPOs pay banks exactly 7% (Jay Ritter data, 2001-2025).
SpaceX fees: about $500 million on a $75B deal (June 2026).
Day one: $135 to $160.95, up 19%, about $14.4B left on the table.
Goldman's equity underwriting was $1.78B of $58.3B in 2025 revenue, about 3%.
Sources: Bloomberg, CNBC, Jay Ritter (Univ. of Florida), Goldman Sachs FY2025 10-K.
News and education, not financial advice.
